name: Split Z Left Z Reverse Right
call: Split Z Left 46 Z Reverse Right
purpose: The Keep Left, until it is not. The quarterback and the near back start the Keep left and never stop selling it; the split man comes back underneath, takes a lateral going the other way and runs right behind the far back. Only the backfield sells it. The line blocks right from the snap, the split man is running backwards behind the line instead of screening anybody, and with him carrying the ball there is one blocker fewer on that edge than Keep Right has going to the same place. It buys a count, not a disguise.

LTE.note: This one takes a long time, and he is quick enough to catch it.

QB.rule: Start the Keep left. Pitch it back underneath — never forward — to the split man crossing your face, then run the Keep like you still have it.

LH.sell: Run your Keep block exactly as always. At half speed, this play dies for good.

Z.rule: Come back behind the line the moment the ball is snapped, take the pitch going the other way, and get outside our end. Stay behind the quarterback until you have it — a pitch that goes forward is a fumble.

coaching_points: This is the Keep Left for the first second and a half, and that is the whole play. Install it the week after the Keep has hurt somebody, never before.
The far back leaves on the same track he leaves on for the Keep — the difference is that this time somebody is following him. The defense cannot tell those two apart, which is the point.
The pitch goes backward. Teach it as a flip to a man running past behind you, not a throw to a man ahead of you.
The near back blocks for a quarterback with no ball. Tell him that out loud, then tell him it is the reason the play scores.
The split man is the slowest-developing ball carrier in the book. If the line cannot hold its blocks for a three count, run Pitch instead.
